# **PHANES Tutorial**

![][image1]

## **1\. Overview**

**PHANES** is an interactive platform for exploring protein properties using a comprehensive set of **physical/chemical, structural, graph-theory, thermostability and expression-derived features** across the human proteome.

The tool enables users to:

* Compare proteins or protein groups  
* Visualize feature distributions and similarities  
* Perform dimensionality reduction analyses (PCA, UMAP)  
* Analyze per-residue and global protein features  
* Compute features directly from uploaded **PDB structures**

---

## **2\. Data Input**

![][image2]

### **🔹 Protein Selection (Primary Input)**

Users can:

* Enter **comma-separated UniProt IDs or Gene names**, or  
* Select proteins from a dropdown list  
* Select gene names  
* Gene Names selects according protein products automatically

---

### **🔹 Secondary Input: “Check Against”**

* Define a second protein group for comparison similar to Protein Selection

---

### **🔹 Feature Selection**

Users can:

* Enter feature names manually, or  
* Select features or feature groups from a dropdown list:  
  * Physical/Chemical  
  * Structural  
  * Graph  
  * Thermostability  
  * Expression

---

### **🔹 PDB File Upload**

* Upload up to **10 PDB files**  
* Compute features and receive results as a **.pkl file**  
* User can optionally insert a valid email in order to get the results

---

## **3\. Analysis Modules**

* All interactive plots include a **“Download Figure”** button to export the visualization  
* Users can also download the **underlying data (filtered by selected UniProt IDs and/or features)** using the **“Download Data”** button

---

##  **3.1 PCA Plot**

### **Description**

Performs **Principal Component Analysis (PCA)** 

Selecting Proteins only in **primary input** highlights these in a PCA of the human proteome

Selecting Proteins in the **secondary input** creates a group of proteins by combining **primary and secondary input** and highlight those in the **primary input**

By clicking a non selected protein in the plot it gets added to the **primary input.** The plot doesn’t rerender automatically.

By clicking the “**Add selected to input**” button, all the selected ids in the current plot or zoomed part of the plot are added to the **primary input**.The user needs to clear **primary input** first.

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** (required)  
* **Secondary Input** (optional)  
* **Feature Selection** (optional, ≥2 features)

### **Output**

* 2D PCA plot  
* Data Table of Selected proteins (**primary and secondary input**) and **selected features**

**![][image3]**

---

## **3.2 UMAP Analysis**

### **Description**

Performs **UMAP**, capturing **non-linear feature relationships** 

Selecting Proteins only in **primary input** highlights these in a UMAP of the human proteome

Selecting Proteins in the **secondary input** creates a group of proteins by combining **primary and secondary input** and highlight those in the **primary input**

By clicking a non selected protein in the plot it gets added to the **primary input.** The plot doesn’t rerender automatically.

By clicking the “**Add selected to input**” button, all the selected ids in the current plot or zoomed part of the plot are added to the **primary input**.The user needs to clear **primary input** first.

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** (required)  
* **Secondary Input** (optional)  
* **Feature Selection** (optional, \>= 2 features)

### **Output**

* 2D UMAP   
* Data Table of Selected proteins (**primary and secondary input**) and **selected features**

**![][image4]**

---

## **3.3 Spider Plot**

### **Description**

Identifies how a selected protein diverges from the human proteome or a user selected protein group by identifying the 5 features that diverge the most by **z-score**. As a result plots a spider (radar) plot of the differences in standard deviations.

Selecting proteins in **Primary input** will use the **first** to evaluate the features and plot the rest.

Selecting proteins in the **secondary input** will construct a group of proteins to serve as the baseline for comparison with the **first protein of the primary input.**

By selecting features in the **feature selection** it will display the selected features.

The User can select how many features to add to the plot up to 10\.

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** (required)  
* **Secondary Input** (optional)  
* **Feature Selection** (optional \<= 10 features)

### **Output**

* Spider (radar) plot of greatest feature differences  
* Data Table of Selected proteins (**primary and secondary input**) and selected features

![][image5]

---

## **3.4 Heatmap Plot**

### **Description**

Displays a Heatmap of selected proteins in the **primary input** and features in the **feature selection**. **Hierarchical clustering** is implemented both for proteins and features based on **euclidean distance**

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** (required)  
* **Secondary Input** ❌ not used  
* **Feature Selection** (required)

### **Output**

* Hierarchically clustered heatmap  
* Data Table of Selected proteins (**primary input**) and **selected features**

![][image6]  
---

## **3.5 Protein Similarity Plot**

### **Description**

Identifies similar proteins in a group, defined by the **primary input** according to features selected in the **feature selection**, by **cosine similarity**.

If the user selects proteins from the **secondary input** then the plot color codes these proteins accordingly.

For visualization, produces a plot of a graph network in which nodes represent proteins and drawn edges represent cosine similarity greater than 0.5.

The user can change the similarity threshold from 0.1 to 1.0

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** (required)  
* **Secondary input** (optional)  
* **Feature Selection** (optional)

### **Output**

* Graph Network plot: Proteins → Nodes / Cosine similarity \>=0.5 → Edges  
* Data Table of Selected proteins (**primary input**) and **selected features**

![][image7]  
---

## **3.6 Violin Plot**

### **Description**

Plots a violin plot of a **single feature** distribution (Kernel Density Estimation)

For proteins selected in the **primary input**, adds horizontal lines to indicate values of selected proteins

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** includes protein specific values (required)  
* **Secondary input** ❌ not used  
* **Feature Selection** (required, single feature)

### **Output**

* Violin plot of KDE distribution, min, max, median, IQR, outliers  
* Data Table of Selected proteins (**primary input**) and **selected feature**

![][image8]  
---

## **3.7 Protein Group Comparison Plot**

### **Description**

Identifies features distinguishing two protein groups by comparing their distributions using **Cohen’s d**. Group 1 and Group 2 are composed of proteins in the **primary** and **secondary input** accordingly. In case of the same Cohen’s d between features **relative difference** serves as a tiebreaker. Plots a scatter plot of **Cohen’s d, relative difference** values **highlighting the top 10 features**.

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** (required, \>=2)  
* **Secondary Input** (required, \>=2)  
* **Feature Selection** ❌ not used

### **Output**

* Scatter plot of ranked features using **Cohen’s d** and **Relative Difference** (in case of tie)  
* Data Table of Selected proteins (**primary and secondary input**)

By clicking a non selected feature in the plot it gets added to the **feature selection.** The plot doesn’t rerender automatically.

By clicking the “**Add selected to input**” button, all the selected features in the current plot or zoomed part of the plot are added to the **feature selection**.

![][image9]

---

## **3.8 Profile Plot**

### **Description**

Visualizes **per-residue feature values** by line plot. Features selected in the **feature selection** should have per-residue feature counterparts (see **Feature Description**)

### **Uses**

* One Protein \- Multiple Features(Up to 12 features) (Domain Consensus)  
* Multiple Proteins \- One feature(Up to 8 proteins) (Domain Comparison)

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** (required)  
* **Secondary input** ❌ not used  
* **Feature Selection** (required)

### **Output**

* Residue-level line plots  
* Data Table of Selected proteins (**primary input**) and **selected feature(s)**

---

## **3.9 Feature Redundancy**

### **Description**

Provides a heatmap of pairwise spearman’s ρ values. These are indicative of the relationships between features as a general step.

User can select features via **feature selection** to specifically illustrate a selected subset.

### **Uses**

* One Protein \- Multiple Features(Up to 12 features) (Domain Consensus)  
* Multiple Proteins \- One feature(Up to 8 proteins) (Domain Comparison)

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** ❌ not used  
* **Secondary input** ❌ not used  
* **Feature Selection** (optional)

### **Output**

* Heatmap with pairwise ρ values

---

## **3.10 Render Table**

### **Description**

By selecting proteins in the **primary input** displays the scalar values of the selected proteins. By selecting features in the **feature selection** displays only the values from the selected features of the selected proteins

### **Input**

* **Protein Selection (primary input)** (required)  
* **Secondary input** (optional)  
* **Feature Selection** (optional)

### **Output**

* Data Table of Selected proteins (**primary input**) and **selected feature(s)**

---

## **3.11 Download Table**

### **Description**

There are multiple ways to populate the data table. Either by rendering a plot or by using the **primary, secondary inputs and feature selection.** By clicking the button the selected data gets downloaded in a csv file

### **Output**

* Csv file with the selected proteins/features.

---

## **4\. Data Download**

### **Global Dataset Downloads**

The complete data can be downloaded as two distinct files.   
phanes\_numeric\_v6\_clean.csv contains scalar data in **csv format**, while   
phanes\_numeric\_v6\_profiles.pkl contains per-residue data in **pkl format** due to large file size.

* **Scalar Data:** profet\_numeric\_v6\_clean.csv  
* **Per-residue Data:** profet\_numeric\_v6\_profiles.pkl

---

### **Plot-Specific Downloads**

For every analysis:

* **Download Figure**  
    Exports the currently displayed visualization  
* **Download Data**  
    Exports the **exact subset of data used in the plot**, based on:  
  * Selected UniProt IDs  
  * Selected features

---

## **5\. Custom Feature Calculation (PDB Input)**

We provide feature calculation for Physical/Chemical, Structural and Graph features. 

For Thermostability Features users can use [https://tools.tartaglialab.com/new\_submission/thermometer](https://tools.tartaglialab.com/new_submission/thermometer) and use the results in Ts\_global\_score.csv

### **Steps**

1. Upload up to **10 PDB files**  
2. Enter email (optional)  
3. Click **Run Analysis**

### **Output**

* Feature values in **.pkl format**
